items.title: Longtime Linux CIFS/SMB3 Maintainer Steps Down
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>There is a changing of the guard with Linux 7.3 as the maintainer of the Common Internet File System (CIFS) / SMB3 code within the Linux kernel. Longtime maintainer, principal Linux CIFS author, and current Microsoft employee Steve French has stepped down due to health reasons...</article>

items.title: Specially Crafted NTFS File-System Image Allows Root Access On Linux With NTFS3 Driver
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>A reported security vulnerability for the NTFS3 driver has gone unaddressed since being reported earlier this summer. The vulnerability allows a pre-crafted NTFS image on a USB flash drive or similar to allow the user to gain root access to the running Linux system...</article>

items.title: AMD RDNA 4m Firmware Published For Linux Ahead Of Launch
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>In addition to AMD's Friday afternoon big code drop of all the UALink enablement patches for the Linux kernel and the AMDGPU driver, there was another big drop from AMD to end out the week... Upstreamed to the linux-firmware.git repository is all the firmware binaries needed by the open-source driver stack for initializing their forthcoming RDNA 4m "GFX 11.7" graphics...</article>

items.title: NVK Vulkan Video Merged For Mesa 26.3
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>The newest major feature to land in Mesa's open-source NVIDIA "NVK" Vulkan driver is support for Vulkan Video!..</article>

items.title: Sched_ext's Sub-Scheduler Support Now "Feature Complete" With Linux 7.3
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>The extensible scheduler framework "sched_ext" that allows for custom schedulers as BPF programs has been working on sub-scheduler support in recent kernel cycles. With Linux 7.3, sub-scheduler support is now deemed feature complete...</article>

items.title: Red Hat's Tuned 2.28 To Improve Out-Of-The-Box WiFi Power Savings On Fedora
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Tuned 2.28 released this Saturday as the newest version of Red Hat's tuning profile delivery mechanism for Linux. Tuned is used notably out-of-the-box on Fedora Linux for monitoring and adaptively tuning systems...</article>

items.title: Open-Source Etnaviv Driver Now Able To Run YOLOX
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>The open-source, reverse-engineered Etnaviv driver stack that began for providing accelerated graphics support on Vivante GPU IP and since expanded to handle Vivante NPUs as well is now able to handle YOLOX object detection...</article>

items.title: Linux 7.3 x86/mm Lands Patches To Greatly Improve Latency-Sensitive Workloads
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>The highlight of this week's x86/mm pull request of changes for the Linux 7.3 kernel are fixes that reduce the time that the TLB flushing code has interrupts disabled. This helps significantly with latency-sensitive workloads but Intel engineer Dave Hansen noted in the pull request that "it's certainly something to keep an eye on" in looking out for any regressions...</article>

items.title: KDE Plasma 6.8 Lands Some Enticing Performance Optimizations This Week
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>This Week in Plasma is out with its latest issue to highlight interesting developments in the trek towards Plasma 6.8...</article>

items.title: OpenZFS 2.4.4 Released With Linux 7.2 Support, Dozens Of Fixes
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>OpenZFS 2.4.4 is out today as the newest stable point release for this ZFS file-system implementation for Linux and FreeBSD systems...</article>

items.title: Wine 11.16 Released With VA-API Hardware Decoding, Better ARM64 Support
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Wine 11.16 is out today as the newest bi-weekly development release for this software enabling Windows games and applications to run on Linux and other platforms...</article>

items.title: Proton 11.0-2 Enables More Titles With Steam Play / Linux Gaming
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Just in time for those that enjoy their Linux / Steam Play gaming on weekends, Valve and CodeWeavers today released Proton 11.0-2 as the newest stable release of this Wine 11.0 downstream that powers Steam Play for running Windows games gracefully on Linux...</article>

items.title: AMD Posts Massive Patch Series For Enabling UALink In The Linux Kernel
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Whether coincidental or intentional, AMD engineers tend to drop interesting, feature patches for the open-source/Linux space on Friday afternoons. Hitting the kernel mailing list minutes ago were two patch series sent out by AMDGPU maintainer Alex Deucher for introducing UALink infrastructure...</article>

items.title: Linux 7.3 Lands Improvements For Voodoo 3 / 4 / 5 & Vintage Atari Computers In 2026
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>At a time when Linux continues dropping older hardware drivers due to the influx of AI/LLM-generated bug reports and patches for hardware extremely unlikely to be used with modern versions of the mainline Linux kernel, Voodoo graphics cards and vintage Atari computers are seeing some reprieve with the upcoming Linux 7.3 kernel release...</article>

items.title: Framework Laptop 16 With GeForce RTX 5070 12GB, One-Piece Keyboard & Haptic Touchpad
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>While the past few weeks have been quite busy with the new Framework Laptop 13 Pro testing with that all-new laptop model and paired with Intel's Core Ultra Series 3 "Panther Lake", at the same time Framework Computer has begun shipping some updated components for the Framework Laptop 16 laptop. If looking for a bit more GPU compute power hor larger form factor than the 13-inch model, the Framework Laptop 16 can now be equipped with the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 GPU as well as a haptic touchpad and one-piece keyboard for improving the input experience.</article>

items.title: Nginx Dark Mode Support For Error Pages Remains Elusive
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>In early 2025 I wrote about the upstream Nginx web server rejecting dark mode support for its error pages on the basis of wanting to keep the default error pages simple and developers arguing the extra HTML tag for the dark mode styling as superfluous. Following a lot of public backlash for being against offering native dark mode handling by default, Nginx stakeholders were polled and largely came out in favor of supporting the functionality but more than one year later it remains elusive from upstream Nginx...</article>

items.title: Intel Computer Vision Sensing Driver Now Ready For Nova Lake
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>The main set of media subsystem updates have been merged for the ongoing Linux 7.3 merge window. Notable this round is the Intel Computer Vision Sensing "CVS" driver merged the previous cycle now supporting next-gen Nova Lake platforms...</article>

items.title: Linux 7.3 Cleans Up Stack Randomization, Ensures It Happen As Early As Possible
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Merged this week for the Linux 7.3 kernel was a big clean-up to the stack randomization code for better security on Linux systems and helping unify some of the architecture-specific code...</article>

items.title: Intel Compute Runtime 26.31.39395.13 Continues Prepping For Crescent Island, OpenCL LEO
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Intel today released the Compute Runtime 26.31.39395.13 open-source GPU compute stack update for Windows and Linux systems. Big ongoing trends for the Intel Compute Runtime continue to be preparing for upcoming Crescent Island and Nova Lake Xe3P graphics hardware as well as building out their new OpenCL LEO driver...</article>

items.title: Linux 7.3 Ready With CXL Type-2 Driver Support For AMD Solarflare NICs
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>With the mainline Linux 7.2 kernel there is now the basic support in place for CXL Type-2 accelerator drivers within the CXL core subsystem code. The first in-tree Type-2 driver with the Linux kernel is for the new AMD Solarflare NIC hardware...</article>

items.title: Linus Torvalds Endures A Debug Session From Hell, "Enormously Helped" By AI
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>It's pretty rare to see Linus Torvalds author patches himself pertaining to the open-source Linux graphics drivers, but waking up this morning I was surprised to see he authored and committed an Intel Xe kernel graphics driver change himself. It ended up being after he encountered a "debug session from hell" but was ultimately helped by AI in fixing a bug that had been irking him...</article>

items.title: Intel Mesa Linux Drivers Now Treating Nova Lake S / U / H / HX As Stable
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Intel's open-source Mesa drivers for Iris Gallium3D (OpenGL) and ANV (Vulkan) on Linux are no longer treating next-gen Nova Lake processors with integrated graphics as experimental and off-by-default. With today's Mesa 26.3-devel code, the Intel driver code across Nova Lake's S, U, H, and HX product families are considered stable and enabled by default...</article>

items.title: Linux 7.3 Network Changes Merged But Developers "Completely Overwhelmed" Due To AI/LLMs
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>All of the networking subsystem feature updates were merged today for the Linux 7.3 kernel's merge window. There are a lot of wired and wireless networking improvements this cycle but also a ton of bug fixes -- including many not so important fixes spun up by AI/LLM agents. The networking subsystem maintainers admit now they are "completely overwhelmed" due to this code churn from the output of AI large language models...</article>

items.title: Rust 1.98 Adds Algebraic Floating-Point Methods Akin To "-ffast-math"
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Rust 1.98 released today and is headlined the debut of new algebraic floating-point methods...</article>

items.title: KMSCON 10.0.2 Brings asciicast Playback Support, Bug Fixes
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>KMSCON 10.0.2 debuted today as the latest update to this leading user-space terminal emulator for Linux systems. KMSCON is built around Linux's KMS/DRM interfaces and the most viable alternative to date for in-kernel VTs...</article>

items.title: KDE Software Now Has Stable Btrfs Snapshot Integration With KIO-Snapshot 1.0
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>With today's release of KIO-Snapshot, KDE software now has stable integration of Btrfs file-system snapshots...</article>

items.title: Intel Hyper Threading Performance On The Xeon 678X "Granite Rapids-WS"
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>With the Intel Xeon 678X "Granite Rapids WS" processor that I have been recently testing within the HP Z4 G6i workstation, there are 48 cores plus with Hyper Threading is a total of 96 threads for this high-end workstation processor with a 300 Watt TDP. For those curious about the performance impact of HT/SMT on this Intel Xeon 600 series workstation processor, here are some comparison benchmarks.</article>

items.title: FSCRYPT Sees Cleanup With Linux 7.3 To Open Door For More Features Like Btrfs Encryption
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>FSCRYPT is the Linux file-system encryption framework for supporting per-directory, transparent encryption. FSCRYPT so far is used by the likes of EXT4, F2FS, and CephFS. For Linux 7.3 there is an important clean-up to the FSCRYPT code to simplify it while also opening the door for new features moving forward into future kernel versions...</article>

items.title: Linux Driver Posted For The PreSonus Quantum 2626: A ~$700 Thunderbolt Audio Interface
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>The PreSonus Quantum 2626 is a high-end, Thunderbolt 3 based audio interface. PreSonus just maintains Windows and macOS drivers for this high-end audio interface while now an open-source Linux driver has been posted after being independently developed via reverse engineering...</article>

items.title: RPM 6.1 Released With Clang Build Fixes, New Release Model
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>RPM 6.1 is out today as the newest feature release for this package management system. With RPM 6.1 comes a number of features and improvements as well as a new release model...</article>

items.title: Mesa 26.2.1 Released With Dozens Of Fixes
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>For those preferring the tradition of waiting for the first point release of a new Mesa feature release before upgrading, Mesa 26.2.1 is available today with a healthy round of bug fixing...</article>

items.title: Linux 7.3 Cleans Up The Code For Disabling Of Legacy 32-bit Time Support
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>The Linux kernel has supported the CONFIG_COMPAT_32BIT_TIME Kconfig build time option for optionally disabling of legacy 32-bit time system call support. This is intended to disable the code that uses a 32-bit integer for time that is thus not Year 2038 safe, but at the cost of breaking compatibility for legacy 32-bit applications. Even if building without Linux 32-bit time support, it turns out some 32-bit time code persisted but that is now being fixed with Linux 7.3...</article>
